Wren 2.6.0 is about keeping the app calm when the machine is busy: the window you are not looking at stops working, scrolling no longer moves the numbers under your finger, and the expensive parts of each sample now happen away from the main thread. Nothing about the interface has been redesigned — it simply stays still and quiet when it should.

## Highlights

- **A hidden window costs almost nothing.** When Wren's window is closed, minimized, hidden, or fully covered by another window, sampling drops to a gentle 20-second rhythm instead of your chosen interval. The menu bar keeps updating and history keeps recording, and reopening the window returns to your chosen rate immediately.
- **The ledger holds still while you scroll.** During a scroll, Wren stops publishing a new snapshot until the gesture ends. Rows can no longer re-sort or change value under your finger, while the background sampler continues recording every sample for the history charts.
- **Hover feedback gets out of the way.** While a list is in motion, hover states change instantly instead of easing, and process names no longer start a 0.28 s text-colour animation for every row the pointer sweeps. The result is a scroll that moves smoothly even on a busy machine.
- **App names and icons are resolved off the main thread.** The LaunchServices lookup and icon read for each process now happen on the sampling queue, once per process, instead of on the main thread. Icons are cached as 20 pt thumbnails at 2×, so drawing a row is a straight copy rather than a large bitmap re-sample.
- **The most expensive hardware reads are paced.** The IOKit registry scan, the network interface walk, and the power-source read now refresh every third tick. Their rates span the longer window, so the numbers stay accurate while each tick does less work.

## Added

- A process-wide scroll activity monitor that recognises trackpad gestures, notched mouse wheels, and keyboard scrolling through both live-scroll and clip-view bounds notifications.
- Window visibility observation for closed, minimized, hidden, and fully occluded states, with a slow background sampling interval that is never written to preferences.
- A cached, pre-scaled process icon thumbnail sized for the ledger at 2× Retina.

## Changed

- The visible snapshot is held for the duration of a scroll; history and menu bar values continue to update in the background.
- Read-hold tracking now publishes only when the set becomes empty or non-empty, so hovering across rows no longer invalidates the toolbar.
- Apps, ledger, and wiki rows skip hover easing while scrolling instead of animating every state change.
- LaunchServices metadata and icon resolution run on the collection queue; `AppSession` applies the already-resolved metadata when it publishes.
- Disk, network, and power readings refresh every third sample, with the first sample always establishing a baseline.

## Fixed

- Intermittent CPU spikes caused by main-thread LaunchServices round-trips and file-backed icon reads during sampling.
- Rows re-sorting and values changing while the reader was scrolling a ledger.
- Toolbar re-evaluation on every row hover, even when no visible state had changed.
- Hover animations keeping the render loop awake and re-rasterizing glyphs throughout a scroll.

## Install

Download `Wren-2.6.0-macOS-arm64.dmg`, open it, and drag Wren to Applications. Requires macOS 14 or later on Apple Silicon.

## First launch (Gatekeeper)

Wren is ad-hoc signed rather than notarized with a paid Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper will say the developer "cannot be verified". Control-click the app, choose **Open**, then **Open** again (or System Settings → Privacy & Security → **Open Anyway**).
